title: Information about school registration
titleCn: 小学入学注册咨询电话

paragraphs.text: Part one.
You will hear a telephone conversation between a man looking for information on registering his child for school and a school district employee.
First, you have some time to look at questions one to six.
Now listen carefully and answer questions one to six.
Good afternoon, Lemon Grove School District.
Hi. I'm calling for information on school registration. I think my son should attend one of the schools in your district.
What grade will your son be entering?
He just turned five. He'll be starting school this year.
Oh, okay. Um, one moment please. I'll get the information for kindergarten registration.
Okay, thank you. Uh, can you give me your address?
Yes, it's seven four one eight Di Marino Street.
Okay, thanks. Yes, at that address, your child should attend Monterey Heights Elementary.
Can you spell that, please?
Yes, it's M-O-N-T-E-R-E-Y Heights.
Great. So how do I register him?

We have registration at each school site Monday through Thursday from nine to one. Oh, no, sorry, one thirty. You'll need to pick up a kindergarten registration packet from the school beforehand, though. It has all the forms you'll need to fill out.
Can I pick up the packet anytime?
Sure. The school office is usually open till three thirty in the afternoons.
Oh, no. I can't really get there that early.
Well, the school has late office hours until four on Thursdays, or I think you can pick up a packet in the school library any day before five.
Oh, okay. I'll stop by there someday this week then before five. Can you tell me what forms we'll need? I'm sure you need his immunization records.

Yes, those, and we also need a general health history signed by your child's doctor, a form filled out by the dentist, emergency contact information, and a residency verification form with proof of residence. Oh, and an original birth certificate.
Okay. That shouldn't be a problem. Can I ask one more question?
Sure, go ahead.
I was wondering about before and after-school care. Do you provide transportation after school?

No, unfortunately, we don't. Parents or caregivers need to pick up the children. There is, however, an on-site licensed daycare for working parents who need after-school care for their children. It's housed within the school grounds, and someone from the daycare will walk to the main school building to pick up your child each day. It's run by the City Youth Council and comes highly recommended.
Can I get information about that as well?
Yes. Uh, flyers and contact information will be included with your packet.
Okay. Thank you.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions seven to ten.
Now listen and answer questions seven to ten.
Oh, and one more thing. I saw a flyer recently for an introduction event for new students and parents, an open house, I think it was called, but I can't remember the date. Was it August third?

That must have been last year's flyer. We haven't put out information on this year's open house yet, but it'll probably be sometime in August. Ah, no. Actually, it will be in July this year since schools start a little early this year. Once your child is registered,
registered, you'll get all that information in the mail, and it'll be on the school website as well.
Great. I'm assuming that during the open house, we get to tour the school and meet our child's teacher.
Yes, and you will set up a time for kindergarten entrance testing as well.
Wow! Testing already. That starts early.
Well, we want to make sure children are properly placed and qualified for special services if necessary.
Okay. I guess that makes sense. Oh, and the first day of school?
The first day will be 19th August . We start in the middle of the week to help with the adjustment. And for kindergartners, the first three days are half days from 8 to 12:30.
Oh, okay. And then the next week, the regular schedule, 8 o'clock to 2:05 will be in force.
Yes, and you can access the full school calendar of holidays and breaks on the school website.
Oh, yeah, I've seen that. The website is very helpful. Thank you so much for your time.
You're welcome, sir.
That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
